safety.title: Safety First
safety.subtitle: All our flights are conducted in accordance with international civil aviation standards.
safety.disclaimer: Those with heart conditions, asthma, pregnancy, or fear of heights must inform us before the flight.

items.q: Do I need experience to paraglide?
items.a: No, you don't need any experience. Our expert pilots will manage the entire process, you just enjoy the view.

items.q: Is there a weight or height limit?
items.a: There is generally a weight limit of up to 110 kg for flights. However, this limit may change depending on wind conditions. If you are over 105 kg, please inform us before booking.
You should prefer comfortable clothes (sneakers, t-shirt/sweatshirt, and a windbreaker depending on the season) and sunglasses. Flights cannot be made with slippers, sandals, or high heels.

items.q: How long does the flight take?
items.a: Our flight time usually varies between 15 and 25 minutes depending on weather and thermal conditions.

items.q: Can I shoot with my phone?
items.a: For safety reasons, you are not allowed to shoot with your personal phones or cameras. Our pilots shoot high-quality footage with professional action cameras.
Pregnant women, people with heart conditions, blood pressure or epilepsy, and those under the influence of alcohol are not suitable to fly.
Anyone aged 4 and above can fly with family consent and permission. We have no upper age limit, any individual in good physical condition can fly.

items.q: What happens if weather conditions are not suitable?
items.a: Flight safety is paramount. If wind or weather conditions are not suitable for flying, your reservation may be cancelled or postponed to another available day/time.

items.q: How far in advance should reservations be made?
items.a: We recommend that you make a reservation at least 2-3 days in advance, especially since it is busy during the summer months.

items.q: What should I do during takeoff?
items.a: You just need to walk or run quickly for a few steps with your pilot's command. You must never jump or sit.
It is a very rare condition. However, if you have a motion sickness problem, you can inform your pilot before the flight that you do not want the optionally offered acrobatic moves.
